description:
The salience-score.py frontmatter-corruption bug root-caused in err-20260828T081109-J571BH (a trailing-newline slicing bug in main()'s frontmatter boundary detection that strands the last line of every salience: block) is still unpatched three cycles later and fired again this cycle exactly as predicted. Both of this cycle's step-01 archives (memory/episodic/dream-summary-2026-08-29.md and memory/episodic/end-of-day-review-2026-08-28-145136.md), written completely clean minutes earlier with a fresh single-line 'salience:
  score: 0' block, came back from step-02's salience-score.py run with the same stranding signature J571BH described: 'related_people:
  - dr-easton
  score: 0
salience:
  score: 10
  last-promoted-check: 2026-08-31' (and 'related_people: []
  score: 0
salience:
...' on the second file). This is the 4th confirmed occurrence of active stranding (APAWBB, NBGENM, J571BH, this entry) despite J571BH proposing a precisely-scoped one-line fix on 2026-08-28 (append the missing trailing newline before slicing, or make the removal regex's trailing group's newline optional). fix_status on J571BH is still 'proposed' -- the script itself has not been touched.
correction: Hand-repaired both affected files in place this cycle (removed the stranded 'score: 0' line from each, leaving the clean trailing salience: block as authoritative) before proceeding to step-03 candidate detection. Also found and hand-repaired a third, worse case while evaluating this cycle's promotion candidates: memory/episodic/shutdown-cleanup-2026-08-07-162834.md (an existing legacy file, not one archived this cycle) carried 12 stacked duplicate 'last-promoted-check:' lines between related_people and its trailing salience: block -- one new orphan added per nightly run from 2026-08-10 through 2026-08-30 -- proving the bug is actively compounding on the pre-existing corpus every night, not only on freshly-archived files. Stripped all 12 orphaned lines, leaving one clean trailing salience: block, before setting promoted:true on it. No corpus-wide repair attempted -- systems/ remains Rigby-gated and this is a capability-level script fix, not a nightly dream-cycle task.
systemic_fix: Same fix J571BH already specified in full detail: patch systems/dream-cycle/salience-score.py's frontmatter slicing to preserve the trailing newline before the removal regex runs (or make the regex's trailing newline optional), and switch parse_frontmatter()'s promoted-detection to the last regex match rather than the first. This entry exists to confirm the bug is still live and unpatched after 3 nightly cycles of the fix sitting proposed, and that it is actively growing on the existing corpus (12-deep on one file found this cycle alone) -- recommend Rigby treat this as due, not merely proposed, given the recurrence count and compounding severity.
